findings.title: CVE-2020-17103 - Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability (Microsoft Security Update Guide)
findings.summary_md: Microsoft's advisory for CVE-2020-17103, an elevation-of-privilege flaw in the Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver (cldflt.sys), was first published on December 8, 2020 as part of the December 2020 security updates, rated Important with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 7.0. Microsoft marked the issue as not publicly disclosed and not exploited at release, and re-released the entry on June 9, 2026 to direct customers to the June 2026 updates after the MiniPlasma proof-of-concept showed the original fix had not held.

findings.title: CVE-2020-17103 Detail - NVD
findings.summary_md: The National Vulnerability Database entry for CVE-2020-17103 records the Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver elevation-of-privilege issue with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.0 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) and lists the weakness as CWE-269. The entry was published on December 10, 2020 and was last modified on June 17, 2026 after the bug re-emerged as MiniPlasma.

findings.title: Hunting for Bugs in Windows Mini-Filter Drivers (Project Zero)
findings.summary_md: James Forshaw's Project Zero post documents the research behind CVE-2020-17103 and three related Cloud Filter and Windows Overlay Filter driver issues, all fixed by Microsoft in December 2020. It explains the cldflt.sys routine that MiniPlasma later re-exploited and how missing access checks in that path let a low-privileged caller act on protected state. The post was published on January 14, 2021.
